step1_figure.circuit_type: Two-stage fully-differential op-amp modified for CMFB input signal
step1_figure.description: Figure 26.26 presents the two-stage fully-differential op-amp with an added NMOS tail transistor for common-mode feedback (CMFB) voltage control. Figure 26.27 illustrates the DC test setup and transfer characteristics of the op-amp outputs as a function of the CMFB control voltage VCMFB.

cmfb_to_output_gain.description: Small-signal voltage gain from the CMFB input (VCMFB) to the op-amp single-ended/common-mode output

equation.explanation: An increase in VCMFB increases the tail bias current of the input diff-amp, raising the first-stage output voltages (vodp, vodm). This reduces the drive of the output buffer PMOS devices, pulling vop and vom downward.
equation.assumptions: Diff-amp and output buffer transistors operate in saturation during transition.

sky130_expected.calculation: In Baker's 1V process, A_{v,CMFB} is approximately 25 (about 10 times lower than the differential forward gain). In SKY130 (VDD=1.8V), with gm ~ 150-250 uS and ro ~ 100-200 kOhm across the two stages, A_{v,CMFB} is expected to be around 15 - 35 V/V.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Lower than differential gain by design to ensure stability of the outer CMFB loop while providing adequate sensitivity.

cmfb_transition_voltage.description: The CMFB bias voltage at which the output switches between high and low rails (point of maximum dVout/dVcmfb)

equation.explanation: Sets the nominal bias point for the CMFB tail device to balance the output stage quiescent operating point near the common-mode level.

sky130_expected.calculation: With Vthn = 0.42V and Vov ~ 0.15V-0.25V, the active transition region occurs around VCMFB = 0.5V to 0.7V for 1.8V supply.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The tail NMOS xm14 turns on when VCMFB exceeds VTHN ~ 0.42V.

output_swing_high.description: Maximum output voltage level when VCMFB is pulled low

equation.explanation: When VCMFB is low, diff-amp current is starved, pulling diff-amp outputs low and turning on output PMOS devices fully.

sky130_expected.calculation: For VDD = 1.8V, VOH reaches near the supply rail limited by the pull-down diode load, typically 1.2V to 1.7V.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Output stage is a push-pull class AB buffer.

output_swing_low.description: Minimum output voltage level when VCMFB is pulled high

equation.explanation: When VCMFB is high, the diff-amp pulls vodp/vodm high, shutting off the output PMOS and pulling the output towards ground.
equation.assumptions: Output NMOS pulls down to triode/saturation boundary.

sky130_expected.calculation: In SKY130 with VDD=1.8V, VOL drops to 50 mV - 250 mV.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Limited by the pull-down current mirror NMOS saturation/triode voltage.

quiescent_current.description: Total quiescent current drawn from VDD under nominal biasing

equation.explanation: There are eight vertical branches in the core op-amp plus bias circuitry, each nominally carrying 20 uA.
equation.assumptions: Each core branch carries ~20 uA at nominal operating point.

sky130_expected.calculation: 8 branches * 20 uA + 50 uA bias = 210 uA nominal. In SKY130 with R1=4k bias network, total quiescent current is around 180 uA - 350 uA.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Consistent with textbook estimation of ~160 uA to 270 uA.

slew_rate.description: Op-amp slew rate set by diff-amp tail current charging compensation capacitor Cc

equation.explanation: Slew-rate limit caused by the diff-amp driving the compensation capacitor.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Direct substitution of design parameters Cc=50fF and 20 uA branch current.

step3_testbench.description: Simulates DC sweep of VCMFB from 0.2V to 1.2V to evaluate CMFB-to-output gain, transition point, and output swing limits, followed by DC operating point analysis to determine quiescent current and power consumption.
